record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.context_brief: Equidistribution of generic special-point Galois orbits
record.original_question: Let {x_n} be a sequence of special points on a Shimura variety, and suppose x_n lies outside any special subvariety for sufficiently large n. Do the Galois orbits of x_n become equidistributed as n→∞ with respect to normalized Haar measure?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 58. Let {xn} be a sequence of special points on a Shimura variety. Suppose that xn lies outside of any special subvariety for sufﬁciently large n. Then the Galois orbits of x n become equidistributed as n → ∞ with respect to the nor-malized Haar measure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a Shimura variety (the canonical model over $\mathbb{C}$ of a Shimura datum $(G,X)$), and recall that a point $x\in S$ is called special if its associated Mumford–Tate group is a torus, and that a special subvariety of $S$ is an irreducible component of the image of a Shimura subdatum. Equip $S(\mathbb{C})$ with its canonical probability measure $\mu_S$ induced by the $G(\mathbb{R})^+$-invariant probability measure on the symmetric domain (the normalized Haar/hyperbolic measure). For a special point $x\in S$, let $O(x)$ denote its Galois orbit under $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/E)$ (where $E$ is the reflex field), and let $\delta_{O(x)}$ be the uniform probability measure supported on $O(x)$.

Let $\{x_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of special points of $S$ such that for every proper special subvariety $Z\subsetneq S$, one has $x_n\notin Z$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Prove or disprove: as $n\to\infty$, the measures $\delta_{O(x_n)}$ converge weakly to $\mu_S$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (equidistribution of generic Galois orbits of special points on Shimura varieties) is a well-known refinement of the André–Oort conjecture due to Clozel–Ullmo. While the André–Oort conjecture itself has been proven unconditionally (Pila–Shankar–Tsimerman et al.), the full equidistribution statement is known in important cases (e.g., CM points on quaternionic Shimura varieties by Clozel–Ullmo, Zhang, and others, and conditionally under GRH via the work of Ullmo–Yafaev) but is not established unconditionally in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Galois orbits and equidistribution of special subvarieties: towards the André-Oort conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds for degrees of Galois orbits and equidistribution of sequences of special subvarieties with bounded Galois orbits, under GRH.
status_evidence.claim: Equidistribution of Galois orbits of special subvarieties is established conditionally (e.g., under GRH) and in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of CM-points on quaternion Shimura varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Equidistribution result for CM points on quaternion Shimura varieties.
status_evidence.claim: Special cases (quaternionic Shimura varieties / CM points) are known.

status_evidence.title: Manin-Mumford, André-Oort, the equidistribution point of view (Ullmo)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing the equidistribution conjecture of Clozel–Ullmo for generic sequences of special points and partial progress.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open in full generality, with partial results.
